text: So without further ado, let's get started.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: My name is Justin Joyce.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: I'm a principal sales operations and strategy manager at Cloudflare.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I work with the go-to-market team as part of the revenue operations organization, specifically on the teams that produce leads for the sales teams, as well as the customer experience team, which works on the customer experience after the sales has been done.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Just a little background about me.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: As Mata said, I started in sales operations and sales, and then I moved to the machine learning side about the last seven years at Grainger.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I really wanted to do that to be able to learn how to have prescriptive analysis and prescriptive predictions so I could help the business better to make decisions and to understand what's the next best step.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Six months ago, I had an opportunity to move back into sales operations because I really wanted to use all the skills that I had been learning from machine learning as well as from sales operations in general.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So what's the general problem?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The general problem is that traditional go-to-market does not scale.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: There's a few facets to this.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The first facet is that usually
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Teams on the back office side, they're either doing work in Excel or Sheets at worst, building analysis each week, multiple hours a week, and as they take on multiple projects, it gets exponentially long with how many of those analysis that they're doing.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: At best, they are producing dashboards, providing information to the leadership and executive team, which meets the needs of most teams, but not all of them.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And that means that, in general, not all the requirements of the go-to-market teams are met.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They're not able to really provide all the information that the teams need when they need it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The second problem, which is more on the go-to-market side with the sales teams and the other teams that I mentioned that I support, is they have two gaps.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Essentially, the first gap is the context gap, meaning when a salesperson is talking to a prospect,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: One call and talking to a current customer in the next call or talking an adoption conversation, the call after that, they have to constantly switch contexts and they have to gather information for those specific calls, which is good.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They really need to get that information to have those calls and understand how to approach the situation, but they have to do all that work in between.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The second one was what I like to call
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: is the expert gap, which is the gap between how your expert salesperson or expert go-to-market sales individual, how he would approach a situation, how he would talk to a prospect, how he would work on an adoption call, how he would handle a customer satisfaction issue, and between also a new salesperson or someone that's just ramping up.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So ideally, like everyone working at the same operational level, so you have consistency
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And execution, consistency, and messaging of how to assess a customer's problems and how your product can help fit that portfolio.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So with these two problems with manual work as well as salespeople not having enough information and having the gap of having to get all the information they need and gather that as well as not being able to execute the same level, it really creates an inefficiency in the go-to-market organization.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so for the last six months or so since I've joined Cloudflare, I've been really focusing on how can I make this operation efficient from back to front.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And there's a lot of great things that we've been doing at our company in general that's helped me enable that.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I really want to share some of those findings with you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the framework that I'm proposing here, which I think is going to really be effective as we flesh this out in the future, is a three-pillar approach.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The first pillar approach is how can we scale analysis and the ability of operations team to meet the data needs of executives, leadership, as well as to be able to build applications using business context.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: How can they take things that would take two hours to do down to five minutes?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Back in January of this year, after I joined the company, I had built these skills, and I started asking questions of the data directly, and I was able to get answers immediately while doing other things.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I saw the huge power of how, if we can scale the analysis and the operations of the teams, we can actually focus on the second part of my job, which is strategy.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The second pillar is to scale insight.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: There's a story in the data, and how can we provide that to the team?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: How can we provide that team at the weekly level, at the different levels of management?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: How can we provide that information, that insight, that story to every customer that these sales teams are talking to?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the third one, which is arguably the biggest one, is to provide self-service capabilities to the go-to-market team.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: When these sales individuals, when they're talking to a customer, how can they get the expert-level information that they need to interact with that customer and to best assess how they should approach the situation, how to handle rejections, how to upsell them, and how to handle customer satisfaction issues?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This is a huge part of what I've seen we've done at Cloudflare, and I'll share in a little bit what that looks like.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So as it relates to scaling the analytical capability, the back office operations, what we have done is we've built role-specific skill files which have the context of this business information tying it to the data.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This is for both technical and non-technical users.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Technical users, you could say the ones who are building SQL and being able to data engineer a lot of solutions.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then the non-technical people will be more individuals who are closer to the business with the salespeople who may not know how to write SQL.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so we have skill files that they're able to use to ask questions of the data to get answers fairly quickly while doing other tasks.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And an example here is in those skill files, we also, through testing, we've included the types of questions that the business would ask of the data.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: In this case, looking at close date changes in opportunities, as well as changes in the amount of the opportunities, so that we can answer essentially 80% or more of the questions, where the other 20% might be more complex strategic questions.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so overall, this allows the teams to be able to embed all of the logic into these skill files and get answers fairly quickly.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So I've seen users who do not know any SQL, and essentially their requests in the past, we bottleneck to someone who knows data and can write SQL for complex queries, be able to just ask questions of the data and get answers.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And this is very useful also for what I show later on the third pillar is for building skills for these go-to-market teams so that they can ask questions of their data and get answers.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Also, in our team, we've used these same skill files to build multiple applications.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: When usually that is done in IT and bottlenecked in those areas, we're able to use the semantic information about the business knowledge as well as the columns to be able to build these applications rather quickly.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So this allows us to free up our time so that we can focus on strategy and enablement.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: For the second pillar, what I mentioned earlier, there's a story in the data, and they really shouldn't have to search for it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: What I'm showing you here is synthetic data on the right.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We have a weekly summary that goes out, which highlights how the business is doing, how they're pacing to their goals, and then highlighting trends, standouts, as well as watches.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This we provide this information to the business so they can as you just like you can open your phone now on Gemini if you have it and you can see your notes for the day or the things that you need to do giving that same level of information to the go to market team so they can just go along their day and if they do need to look at some of the reports or dashboards they can to drill in but we bring the story to them.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I'll pull this together why I think this is really important.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Of course, there's a place for dashboards in standardized information, but there's a different level of adoption of the KPI metrics at any given company.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You're going to have people who love dashboards.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: People are never going to look at them.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So I think you really need to have a way to scaffold that across
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The business.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So how do we do this automated analysis?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So a big part of this is simplifying the data so that the AI agents can actually analyze the data in a very consistent and clean way.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Here what we do is we transform the data by the dimension of time, also slice of the logical part of the business, which is manager, theater, and finally the metric.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Here we have data that is wide.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You could also go from wide to long.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Our trend information that I showed you,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That data is long, and then we do some pre-processing on that data to then highlight trends.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the embedding of the logic of how you would filter this data to even analyze it, as well as the logical aggregations the business would want to see, is all engineered up front.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: From my experience, this handles 80-plus percent of the requests.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It's just getting information about the performance of the teams and how they're doing.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You can always go down to the raw data, but this last pillar, which I'll go over in a minute, allows them to do that.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: To be able to orchestrate this effectively and be able to rely on it, we have a multi-agent workflow where we first get the data, and then we do a first-pass draft on the data, calling our MCPs.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we have a second reviewer agent who checks the veracity of the data.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we have a third agent, which is a tone agent who, using a multi-shot prompt, is able to craft the message and highlight the risks and opportunities equally.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And with every run, we have observability into each of the LLM calls, so we can see what is passed and what is the response that is going on there.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so this architecture we tested for about two, three months and, you know, looking at every single run to see what is going wrong.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And this is the model that we had set up that is really working for us.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we really hope to expand this beyond just what I've shown you for multiple teams, but also down to the customer level like I was just talking to you about.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The third part is the self-service model.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And what I'm showing you here is our internal tool called Cloudflare OS, which is an agentic workspace that is running on Cloudflare, where the go-to-market team can come in here.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It spins up their own compute and their own persistent environment using Cloudflare workers as well as durable objects, which is basically a storage, sort of like S3.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so the salespeople can come in here and get the data that they need it when they need it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So some use cases that these teams are using it for is doing a forecast brief, building QBR decks, building a purchase deck on what the customer that they're onboarding has purchased, doing account planning, general queries of the data, as well as renewal preparation.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: How are they going to look at what the customer has used and either upsell them or figure out how they can get them adopting their product more?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So just a little bit more into that Cloudflare S setup that I just showed you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The AI Agent Workspace is that screen I was showing you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And through the three-part piece of the skills in the lower left, which is our expert-level information,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: as well as the MCP connection and the AI gateway.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They're able to have conversations in this agentic workspace to pull data they need and using expert level skills which is curated so that they are able to execute the jobs that they need to do when they need to do it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so a little more information about the skill repository.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We have a central alias where skills are presented to the central team, curated by the go-to-market team as well as by operations team, and they're reviewed so we can make sure that we're not having a proliferation of skills, and we have an expert-level knowledge skill at every level so that they can really get all the information they need for how to approach any customer situation.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so just a few more images here of them using it.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Here we have them building a prescriptive plan for their daily work.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They're asking a question.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You can see the agent is responding by looking into the MCP and starting to pull the data together.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And related to the QBR deck, here's a slide of generating a custom slide deck for a customer call.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so this has really, I think, unlocked the ability of the go-to-market teams to be able to really have all their information service to them.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so bring it together with the three pillars that I talked about.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If you really don't have all these, I think you have issues with serving the go-to-market needs in terms of optimizing the use of agentic systems.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: With self-service, you allow them to be able to pull data when they need it for whatever situation they need it with the expert-level information.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The second is by pushing the insights to the business, you're able to surface the generalized, standardized information of how these teams are doing and also so they're aligning with source of truth on performance.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then the third one is the scaling of the analytical team for them to be able to answer queries and build applications for the teams, which really unlocks a lot because the opportunity cost of that team being overloaded and being able to help is that the needs of the go-to-market team is not met.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So some findings in the future.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the first thing is skill curation is the basis for all of this agentic workforce.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If you're able to embed the knowledge of the business into these skill files, as well as the skills for the analyst to be able to answer questions or build applications, as well as those skills that I showed you in the Cloudflare OS,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You're really able to give them the ability to use the agentic systems in a more predictable and deterministic way so that they can execute evenly across the board.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the second thing is through this whole process, the feedback loop is very important.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Just like a company would try to sell a product externally and get feedback with these internal teams, the feedback loop is very important to be able to see is what you're building is actually useful, what are some issues that they're having, and how can you make this work more efficiently.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the third thing is the layering of those three pillars that I talked about, being able to answer questions where the team comes to you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Some of the go-to-market team, that's how they like to interface with the operations team is to be able to ask questions.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then the pushing of information and the self-service ability, through that you're able to interweave all the needs of the team to be able to be met by this agentic run team.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So through all these
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Different pillars that I talked about, we've really been able to 2X our efficiency and be able to serve the teams as well as allowing them to be able to get the information that they need to do their job.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so some things that I see going into the future, number one is a deeper integration with our systems that we work in.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I see that being set up in a way that I set up with the automated analysis where you have multi-agent workflows to just make sure that everything is getting done right.

text: And the second thing is we're sort of reached the Cambrian stage of using agentic systems, which means there's an explosion of excitement and skills and finding out ways to solve anything with AI.
